title: Salt Flats
statement: A series about the flat, white silence of the Atacama salt pans, printed in two inks so the paper does the rest of the work.

title: The Quiet Hours
statement: Cover and chapter openers for a novel about a night porter. Every image is lit by one lamp.

title: Heat
statement: A festival poster for a summer of outdoor cinema. One colour, one shape, and a sun that is slightly too big.

title: Public Library Week
statement: Three posters for a city-wide library campaign. The grid is borrowed from a card catalogue.

title: Field Notes 4
statement: A quarterly about urban nature. This issue follows one hedgerow through a year, with pacing that slows down for winter.

title: Letters from Home
statement: An essay about migration told through family letters, designed so the letters sit on the page like objects.

title: Tidal
statement: Long exposures of the same rock pool at every tide over one month.

title: After the Rain
statement: A street in the minute after a summer storm, when everyone is still inside.

title: Hartwell Grotesk
statement: A grotesque drawn from hand-painted shop signs, with a text cut that stays open at small sizes.

title: Orchard
statement: A rounded display face drawn for a cider maker, with alternates that echo the shape of the apples.

title: Pressure
statement: A looping poster about deadlines that tightens a little every time you look at it.

title: Atlas of Small Things
statement: An atlas of objects found within ten steps of the studio door, each drawn at actual size.

title: Night Ferry
statement: A crossing at night, told in one image. The jury called it the quietest picture in the room, and the one they kept returning to.

title: Low Tide Almanac
statement: A year of tide tables turned into a book you want to read, with a type system that changes with the moon.

title: Rumble
statement: A poster for a drum festival. The letter shakes if you stand in front of it long enough.

title: A Year of Weather
statement: 365 days of temperature and rain in one diagonal, designed for a newspaper back page.

title: Migrations
statement: Starlings over the coast at dusk, shot from the same rooftop for six weeks.

title: Gather
statement: A friendly slab for community signage, tested on real noticeboards before release.

title: Second Sun
statement: A sunrise drawn as if seen twice. The jury praised its patience and its colour.

title: Glasshouse
statement: A botanic garden reopening poster, where the rings are the growth lines of a tree.

title: The Night Shift
statement: A portrait of a hospital porter at 4 am, lit by a vending machine.

title: Garden City
statement: A cover about city gardens where every dot is a planted plot.

title: Ground Floor
statement: A student series about the shops at street level, built on a checkerboard of opening hours.

title: A is for Arches
statement: Lettering based on the arches of a market hall, used on its new signs.
